title: Boss: work nobody is waiting for
summary: A report that ignores cancellation, a legacy client with no token, and a hedged request that cancels the loser.

steps.title: The ticket
body: **PERF-912: database CPU stays at 90% for minutes after a traffic spike ends.**
info: Reports[0] yearly report computed in 212004 ms (client already gone)
warn: Legacy.Ftp[0] transfer still running 15 min after request was cancelled
info: Search[0] p99 4.8 s; 2% of calls to search-eu take > 4 s; the rest finish in 40 ms
`499` is the client closing the connection. The work went on anyway. Make every piece stop when nobody is waiting, and cut the
search tail latency with a **hedged** request.

steps.title: 1. A CPU loop that listens
prompt: Write **`static long SumOfSquares(IEnumerable<int> values, CancellationToken ct)`** returning the sum of `v * v` (as `long`).
- Check the token **before the first item and then every 1,024 items** with `ct.ThrowIfCancellationRequested()`;
checking on every item is wasteful, checking never ignores the client.
The tests cancel the token while the 2,000th item is produced and count how far your loop read after that.
starter: static long SumOfSquares(IEnumerable<int> values, CancellationToken ct)
foreach (var v in values) sum += (long)v * v;
solution: static long SumOfSquares(IEnumerable<int> values, CancellationToken ct)
template: IEnumerable<int> DojoValues() { for (var i = 1; i <= 100_000; i++) { dojoRead = i; if (i == 2000) dojoCts.Cancel(); yield return i; } }
Dojo.Throws<OperationCanceledException>("Cancelling mid-way stops the loop", () => SumOfSquares(DojoValues(), dojoCts.Token));
Dojo.Check("It stops within 1,024 items of the cancellation", dojoRead <= 2000 + 1025, $"It read {dojoRead} items.");
IEnumerable<int> DojoCount() { for (var i = 0; i < 5000; i++) { dojoTouched++; yield return i; } }
Dojo.Throws<OperationCanceledException>("An already cancelled token stops it before any work", () => SumOfSquares(DojoCount(), dojoEarly.Token));
Dojo.Check("Checks before the first item", dojoTouched <= 1, $"It read {dojoTouched} items first.");
hints: Keep a counter `i`; when `i % 1024 == 0`, check the token. With `i++` inside the condition, item 0 is checked too.
`if (i++ % 1024 == 0) ct.ThrowIfCancellationRequested();` at the top of the loop body.

steps.title: 2. A legacy client without tokens
prompt: `LegacyClient.ReadAsync()` takes no token, but it has `Abort()`, which makes the pending read fail with
Write **`static async Task<string> ReadAsync(LegacyClient client, CancellationToken ct)`**:
- on cancellation call `client.Abort()` (use `ct.Register`), and throw `OperationCanceledException` (not the `IOException`);
- **dispose the registration** when the read is over, so a later cancellation does not abort the next read on the same client;
starter: static async Task<string> ReadAsync(LegacyClient client, CancellationToken ct)
solution: static async Task<string> ReadAsync(LegacyClient client, CancellationToken ct)
template: await Dojo.ThrowsAsync<OperationCanceledException>("Cancelling aborts the read with OperationCanceledException", () => dojoRead);
Dojo.Eq("A read that is not cancelled returns the text", "report.csv", await dojoOk);
Dojo.Eq("After the read, cancelling no longer aborts the client", 0, dojoClient2.Aborts);
hints: `using var registration = ct.Register(client.Abort);` before awaiting: the `using` disposes it when the method ends.
Wrap the await in `try { ... } catch (IOException) when (ct.IsCancellationRequested) { throw new OperationCanceledException("read cancelled", ct); }`.

steps.title: 3. A hedged request
prompt: Two replicas serve search. Most calls are fast; a few hang for seconds. **Hedging** cuts that tail: if the primary has not answered
after a short delay, ask the secondary too, take whichever answers first, and cancel the other.
Write **`static async Task<string> HedgedAsync(Func<CancellationToken, Task<string>> primary, Func<CancellationToken, Task<string>> secondary, TimeSpan hedgeAfter, CancellationToken ct)`**:
- start `primary`; if it finishes within `hedgeAfter`, return its result and **never call** `secondary`;
- otherwise start `secondary` as well and return the result of whichever finishes first;
- **cancel the other one** (give both calls a token you cancel at the end);
- if `ct` is cancelled, the calls are cancelled too.
starter: static async Task<string> HedgedAsync(Func<CancellationToken, Task<string>> primary, Func<CancellationToken, Task<string>> secondary, TimeSpan hedgeAfter, CancellationToken ct)
solution: static async Task<string> HedgedAsync(Func<CancellationToken, Task<string>> primary, Func<CancellationToken, Task<string>> secondary, TimeSpan hedgeAfter, CancellationToken ct)
template: async Task<string> DojoHang(CancellationToken ct) { dojoPrimaryToken = ct; await Task.Delay(Timeout.Infinite, ct); return "never"; }
Task<string> DojoSecondary(CancellationToken ct) { dojoSecondaryCalls++; return Task.FromResult("from secondary"); }
Dojo.Eq("A fast primary answers", "from primary", await HedgedAsync(DojoFast, DojoSecondary, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2), CancellationToken.None));
Dojo.Eq("The secondary is not called when the primary is fast", 0, dojoSecondaryCalls);
Dojo.Eq("A hanging primary is hedged by the secondary", "from secondary", await HedgedAsync(DojoHang, DojoSecondary, TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(20), CancellationToken.None));
Dojo.Check("The losing primary is cancelled", dojoPrimaryToken.IsCancellationRequested, "Give the calls a token from a linked source and cancel it once there is a winner.");
var dojoTask = HedgedAsync(DojoHang, DojoHang, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5), dojoCaller.Token);
await Dojo.ThrowsAsync<OperationCanceledException>("Cancelling the caller cancels the calls", () => dojoTask);
hints: Use a linked `CancellationTokenSource` for both calls. `await Task.WhenAny(first, Task.Delay(hedgeAfter, token))` tells you whether the primary was fast.
After starting the secondary: `var winner = await Task.WhenAny(first, second); cts.Cancel(); return await winner;`.
explain: Hedging trades a little extra load (only for slow calls) for much better tail latency. Only hedge **idempotent** reads: a hedged
payment could charge twice. `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience` has a ready-made hedging handler (`AddStandardHedgingHandler`).
